title: Horizon and Machine
premise: Hazel Montrose, a xenolinguist whose mind has rewired itself around alien grammar until she no longer dreams in human languages, pilots the long-haul freighter Perihelion between colonies that have gone linguistically dark. When a manifest update lists her dead brother's name aboard the Meridian—a ship that never flew—she traces it to an orbital station where two cryo-banks hold the last survivors of a sabotaged generation ship: one bank holding the engineers who built the sabotage, one holding its victims. The reactor powering both banks is failing, and only half can be woken before the countdown ends. Hazel must choose which half of humanity wakes, uncovering that her brother is alive in the wrong bank and that her own family's fortune was built on the crime. She wakes the victims, lets the perpetrators sleep into death, and carries her brother home to a world she has finally learned to dream in again.
about_author: C. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. They write about people who keep languages alive the way sailors keep lights burning.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Aboard the Perihelion, Hazel delivers cargo to Kestrel Station, where the colonists have stopped answering in any language she recognizes. She translates for them by instinct rather than study, and realizes with quiet grief that she dreamed last night in a syntax no human ever spoke. Beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Name That Should Be Dust
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine manifest sync flags Elias Montrose—her brother, dead twelve years—as a registered passenger on the Meridian, a generation ship officially scrapped before launch. Her inquiries are stonewalled by the Shipping Authority within hours. Beat: the past reaching up through paperwork.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with interludes from station archivist Bo Okonkwo. Following forged records to the derelict Meridian's drydock, Hazel finds the hull intact and crewed by ghosts of data: launch logs, a sealed cryo-bay, and a reactor counting down from four hundred days. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Banks
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Bo reveals the truth: the Meridian flew in secret, was sabotaged en route, and limped back; its survivors were split into two cryo-banks pending a tribunal that never convened. One bank holds the saboteurs' faction, one their victims—including, impossibly, Elias. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Family Built
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging into the Montrose estate, Hazel finds her parents' shipping fortune was financed by the Meridian consortium—and that her mother signed the order burying the investigation. The inheritance she has lived on is blood money. Beat: betrayal turning inward.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hacking the cryo-banks' diagnostic feeds, Hazel hears recorded final messages from both factions—the perpetrators unrepentant, the victims singing to stay sane. Her alien-trained ear catches something in the victims' song: a coded ledger naming every saboteur. Beat: grief becoming evidence.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The reactor's failure accelerates; power remains for one bank only. The Shipping Authority arrives not to help but to erase the site, offering Hazel a bribe and her brother's freedom if she stays silent. Beat: the law revealed as another kind of crime.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Refusing the deal, Hazel broadcasts the coded ledger to every colony on her long route, letting the victims' own voices name their murderers across inhabited space. The Authority moves to seize the station by force. Beat: defiance at full voice.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. In the reactor's final hour, Hazel chooses: she wakes the victim bank, including Elias, and seals the saboteurs' bank behind a manual lock as the second reactor fails. Elias wakes not knowing he was saved or condemned by the same hand. Beat: sacrifice and reunion colliding.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Human
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Hazel and Elias fly the long route together, delivering the tribunal verdicts colony by colony. On Kestrel Station, Hazel dreams for the first time in years in her mother tongue—and finds she still remembers the aliens' grammar too. Beat: inheritance remade as chosen family.
